findings.claim: The public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

verifier.reason: GroupsController#members now unconditionally defaults to limit=50 for all groups (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26) and Discourse.Group#findMembers sends limit: 50, offset: 0 (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10-29). The public group members route only calls model.findMembers() once (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12) and its template renders members with no pagination or load-more controls (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1-21), so members beyond the 50th cannot be reached.

findings.claim: In the group member row itemView, {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the member (Discourse.User) rather than the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the remove link is shown for automatic groups.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:21 uses the keyword form `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so Ember's collectionHelper (vendor/assets/javascripts/development/ember.js:7997-7998) binds the itemView's `_context` to `_parentView.context` (the AdminGroupController / group) rather than `content`, while exposing the Discourse.User only via the `member` keyword (ember.js:8223-8225). Thus `{{#unless automatic}}` in app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 resolves against the group controller and hides the remove link for automatic groups.

findings.claim: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' controller spec sends xhr :put to remove_member, but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing.

verifier.reason: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:114-116, the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`, whereas config/routes.rb:49-50 maps `DELETE members` to `groups#remove_member` (and `PUT members` to `groups#add_members`). Because Rails controller specs dispatch directly to the named action without enforcing HTTP verb routing, the spec passes despite using the wrong verb.

findings.claim: The limit and offset params on the members endpoint are not validated or clamped: negative values reach SQL and cause errors, and limit has no upper cap.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without lower-bound validation or an upper cap, so negative values generate invalid negative SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` clauses in PostgreSQL and arbitrary positive `limit` values are uncapped. The patch rewrote these lines and removed the `if group.automatic?` guard, exposing all groups to this unvalidated input.

findings.claim: The usernames input is not cleared after an add operation.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65, the addMembers action passes this.get("usernames") to the model's addMembers method without clearing usernames or resetting the user-selector input, even leaving a '// TODO: should clear the input' comment at line 62. Neither Discourse.Group#addMembers (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60) nor the user-selector component clears the input afterwards.
